messages:
peter: after running the linux installer (deb) on my devbox, `redwoodctl local-test up` fails with `open /etc/redwood/config.yaml: permission denied`. installer said it wrote config to /etc/redwood.
anika: hmm installer should write a system config only for system-wide installs. did you run the .deb with sudo?
peter: yes, installer asked for sudo. I expected it to create per-user files in ~/.config/redwood but now the process (running as my user) can't read /etc/redwood/keys.pem. `strace` shows EACCES on open.
morgan: that rings a bell. last release added an optional global config to make multi-user shared machines easier but the postinstall script had a bug: it wrote files with 0640 and root:root ownership, no group. so unprivileged users can't read keys.
infra-bot: created issue infra#8822 "installer: system config file permissions prevent user runtime from reading keys" (detected 5 installs in last week).
peter: workaround I used: `sudo chown root:redwood /etc/redwood && sudo chmod 0640 /etc/redwood/config.yaml && sudo setfacl -m u:$USER:r /etc/redwood/keys.pem` — not great for onboarding.
anika: we should avoid requiring users to mess with ACLs. Proposed fixes: (1) installer create a `redwood` group and add the installing user into it when prompted, (2) write files with 0644 for non-secret files and 0640 for keys with group set to `redwood`, (3) for single-user installs default to `~/.config/redwood` unless `--system` flag passed.
morgan: agreed. also add a runtime check: if config file unreadable due to perms, produce a clear diagnostic: "Permission denied reading /etc/redwood/config.yaml. Did you run a system install? Try `sudo redwoodctl init --system` or run `redwoodctl init --user` to create per-user config." Right now we just error with EACCES and a stack trace.
peter: +1. My error had no actionable hint and I spent 20m figuring out it was permission bits.
karthik: small edge-case: in some enterprise images the os image is baked with /etc/redwood owned by root:redwood and installers add user to `redwood` group, but group membership doesn't apply until next login. installer should detect that and remind user to re-login or suggest `newgrp redwood` or add the current user to group in the same shell session.
manifest-bot: note: tickets created: installer#921 "create redwood group + safe perms", cli#901 "friendly error on unreadable system config".
morgan: i'll send a hotfix to the deb postinst to default to per-user config unless `--system` flag present and update RPM/PKG scripts. also update docs: "system install implications and permissions".
anika: for now add a CLI fallback: if /etc/redwood present but unreadable, fallback to ~/.config/redwood and print a banner: "Found system config but cannot access; using per-user config. To fix system install, run sudo chown -R root:redwood /etc/redwood and add users to the redwood group."
peter: that fallback unblocked me instantly. thanks. also added a tiny note to our onboarding doc so new hires won't hit this.
karthik: i'll follow up with packaging team to ensure installer sets group and optionally adds user. leaving a comment on installer#921 with the `newgrp` suggestion.
morgan: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/77 "deb: default to per-user config; safe group perms for /etc/redwood". includes tests for RPM/DEB postinst.
\pin: thanks team, this would've been a rough support call otherwise. :thumbsup:
